title: ThedaCare, Inc. v. Ascension NE Wisconsin, Inc.
citation: Outagamie County Circuit Court, Wisconsin, No. 2022CV000068, Doc. 11 (January 2022)
lead: A healthcare team’s planned move prompts an initial temporary order giving the new employer a staffing alternative; the instrument does not resolve employment rights on the merits.

actors.name: ThedaCare, Inc.
actors.role: Employer seeking temporary relief when seven team members planned to leave.

actors.name: Ascension NE Wisconsin, Inc.
actors.role: Prospective new employer and defendant subject to the temporary order.

actors.name: Seven team members
actors.role: Amber Kohler, Andrew Kohler, Samantha Baltus, Timothy Breister, Kailey Young, Michael Preissner and Paul Winter.

proceedings: ThedaCare sought temporary relief against Ascension.
Judge McGinnis signed document 11 on January 20, 2022; it was filed January 21.
The recovered instrument covers only that initial temporary restraining order.
limits: The signed order contains no developed merits reasoning and does not establish permanent enforceability, an employee noncompetition promise or present effect. Later dissolution or other proceedings require their own sources. The complaint’s poaching characterization remains an allegation.

review.basis: Individually written and compared with the canonical full brief; no new independent opinion audit claimed.

sections.title: Seven healthcare workers plan to move to another employer
sections.cue: What did the former employer allege?
paragraphs: The assigned account describes members of ThedaCare’s interventional radiology and cardiovascular team seeking to join Ascension NE Wisconsin during the pandemic. The textbook frames their employment as at will and asks what follows from treating such workers as essential. ThedaCare’s complaint accused Ascension of poaching them; that accusation was the employer’s allegation, not an adjudicated finding of unlawful conduct.

The seven people named in the later order were Amber Kohler, Andrew Kohler, Samantha Baltus, Timothy Breister, Kailey Young, Michael Preissner and Paul Winter. ThedaCare sought a temporary restraining order against Ascension.

sections.title: The circuit judge grants temporary relief against Ascension
sections.cue: What did the written instrument actually address?
paragraphs: Outagamie County Circuit Judge Mark J. McGinnis electronically signed the temporary restraining order on January 20, 2022, and it was filed January 21 as document 11 in case 2022CV 000068. The order granted ThedaCare’s motion based on the filings and evidence submitted and cited Wisconsin Statutes § 813.02.

Its command addressed Ascension, the named defendant. It was not an employment-contract judgment entered against the individual workers, and it did not reproduce the contracts, Ascension’s response or the evidence underlying the request.

sections.title: Ascension receives a staffing-or-hiring choice
sections.cue: How did the two alternatives limit the command?
paragraphs: Under the first alternative, Ascension could make one invasive radiology technician and one registered nurse from the named group available to ThedaCare, including support for on-call responsibilities. Under the second, Ascension could cease hiring the named individuals until ThedaCare hired adequate replacement staff for the departing team members.

The order therefore provided a staffing alternative and tied the hiring restriction to replacement staffing. It did not fix a number of days or directly order the employees to work indefinitely for ThedaCare. It made violations by Ascension immediately punishable by contempt and continued the order unless and until a subsequent court order terminated it.

sections.title: The initial order leaves the underlying employment merits unexplained
sections.cue: What can be concluded from this stage alone?
paragraphs: The two-page instrument supplied no developed findings explaining why temporary relief was justified. It did not identify an enforceable promise by a worker, decide that anyone lost the right to quit, or establish a general no-poaching or tortious-interference rule. No judicial footnotes, separate opinions or appendices appeared.

The exact result was a grant of the temporary restraining motion subject to the two alternatives and contempt enforcement. It was not a permanent injunction or final damages award. The order’s continuation clause described its interim operation at issuance; it does not establish that the restraint remains effective now. Later hearings, dissolution or final resolution are outside this recovered instrument.

sources.pinpoint: Limited reasoning and exact disposition; order1–2
